aboutH2: TeDDs on Chapel: a five-client recovery program in Grand Falls
intro: TeDDs on Chapel Center for Recovery is a small private addiction program in Grand Falls (Grand-Sault), in New Brunswick's upper Saint John River valley. It treats adults for alcohol and drug addiction and never has more than five clients at a time. You can choose a 21, 30 or 42 day program and do it as a residential stay, online, or as a hybrid.

The approach comes from the neuroscience of addiction. Counsellors explain what alcohol and drugs have done to the brain, why cravings are so strong, and how the brain recovers through neuroplasticity. The centre keeps a low profile on purpose, with no sign outside, and it has a particular focus on doctors, nurses and other licensed professionals who need treatment kept private.

pillars.title: Five People at a Time in Grand Falls
pillars.body: TeDDs runs out of a private house in Grand Falls, the bilingual town on the Saint John River near the Quebec and Maine borders. The photos the centre shares show a lounge with a pellet stove, a sitting room, a full kitchen and a renovated bathroom, and its recovery.com profile lists private or shared air-conditioned rooms with a desk and TV. With five clients at most, the house never feels like an institution. The centre puts it simply: you are welcomed as a visitor, not a client in a rehab.

pillars.title: Treatment Built on How Addiction Changes the Brain
pillars.body: The TeDDs model maps how addiction develops over a lifetime and matches those brain changes to behaviour, before and during substance use. Clients learn why the habit has such a hold and why it continues even when they know the damage. Counselling is one on one, with cognitive behavioural therapy and nutrition counselling listed on recovery.com. Each day includes biofeedback-assisted meditation that records stress levels, and an exercise class designed by Olympic and professional coaches and led by a certified trainer.

pillars.title: A Phone Call Away When the Program Ends
pillars.body: TeDDs tells clients it stays a call away for advice and support once the program is over. For licensed professionals, it can write letters of support for a return to work. The centre's recovery.com profile lists support meetings, outpatient treatment, professional re-entry support and employment counselling as aftercare. Because the program also runs online, clients from elsewhere in New Brunswick or across Canada can keep working with the same counsellors from home.

overview: Days at TeDDs mix education, counselling and physical recovery. Clients get an initial assessment and are monitored as they adjust to life without alcohol or drugs. Meals are organic. Counsellors spend time on shame and guilt, and on how to rebuild trust with family, friends and colleagues, without tying the program to any religious belief.

location.heading: TeDDs on Chapel Center for Recovery in Grand Falls, New Brunswick
location.intro: TeDDs on Chapel is in Grand Falls (Grand-Sault), a bilingual town on the Saint John River in northwestern New Brunswick, about 40 minutes from Edmundston and close to the Quebec and Maine borders. Fredericton is about 2 hours away by the Trans-Canada Highway, Saint John about 3 hours and Moncton roughly 4 hours.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's own website and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: What kind of program is TeDDs on Chapel?
faqs.a: TeDDs on Chapel is a small private addiction program in Grand Falls, New Brunswick, for adults dealing with alcohol or drug addiction. It offers residential, virtual and hybrid programs, and recovery.com also lists outpatient care. No more than five clients are in the program at once.
TeDDs runs 21, 30 and 42 day programs. Each length is available as a residential stay, an online program or a hybrid of both. The right one is worked out with you during the free consultation.

The centre is in the town of Grand Falls (Grand-Sault) in northwestern New Brunswick. That is about 2 hours by car from Fredericton, around 40 minutes from Edmundston and roughly 4 hours from Moncton. The centre does not publish a street address and has no sign, so you get directions when you book.
TeDDs does not publish its prices. Cost depends on the program and the length of stay, so you need to call for a quote. The centre is private pay and no insurance providers are listed.

No. TeDDs on Chapel does not provide medical detox. If you need help with withdrawal, you have to arrange that before the program starts. Recovery.com also lists no sober living or in-home care at the centre.

Treatment is based on the neuroscience of addiction and the idea that the brain can heal through neuroplasticity. It uses one-on-one counselling, cognitive behavioural therapy, education about how addiction develops, nutrition counselling and daily biofeedback-assisted meditation. Clients also get neurocognitive testing through Cambridge Brain Sciences to track progress.

faqs.q: Is TeDDs suitable for doctors, nurses and other licensed professionals?
faqs.a: Yes, TeDDs says its program was designed with licensed professionals in mind. There is no signage, notes are returned to you when you leave, and the centre says it is not required to report to outside agencies. It will write letters of support if you ask.

faqs.q: Can I do the program online?
faqs.a: Yes. The 21, 30 and 42 day programs can be done online or as a hybrid of online and residential time. Recovery.com also lists online therapy and virtual care for the centre.

faqs.q: What support is there after the program?
faqs.a: TeDDs says it stays a phone call away for advice and support after you finish. Its recovery.com profile lists support meetings, outpatient treatment, professional re-entry support and employment counselling as aftercare.
Call (506) 702-5032 for a free, confidential telephone consultation, or use the contact form on teddsonchapel.com. The centre is small, so ask about start dates early.
